articles.title: The secret to a perfect crystal may be a precisely calibrated extra turn
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Creating a perfect crystal sounds straightforward: Arrange identical building blocks into a repeating, orderly structure. At the microscopic scale, though, even subtle biases in how particles interact can push them in preferred directions, making it harder to form uniform crystalline materials.

articles.title: Queasy plesiosaurs swam to shore to vomit, Jurassic fossils reveal
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Plesiosaurs swam into river deltas to vomit up shells and other indigestible elements of their marine meals, suggests new research published by Cambridge University Press. The behavior resembles that of today's fur seals and marine crocodiles.

articles.title: Injectable nanoparticles make blind retinas respond to light in preclinical study
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: An international research team has developed microscopic particles that can make blind retinas respond to light. The particles act as tiny light receptors. Researchers inject them into the eye, where they settle close to nerve cells in the retina. When light hits the particles, it triggers electrical and chemical processes that can activate the nerve cells and prompt them to send signals toward the brain.

articles.title: The end of humanity? What would happen if the Yellowstone supervolcano erupted now
articles.summary: A Yellowstone super-eruption would begin not with a sudden surprise, but with weeks of increasingly alarming warning signs such as migrating earthquake swarms, rapid ground uplift, changing geysers, and rising volcanic gases. In a worst-case scenario, those signals could culminate in a VEI 8 eruption that blasts ash tens of kilometers into the atmosphere, unleashes deadly pyroclastic flows, buries parts of the western United States in ash, and cripples transportation, electricity, water systems, agriculture, and communications across much of North America.
